name: Good Speech (Qawl Sadid / Kalima Tayyiba)

definition_by_age.4: Using kind words when you talk.
definition_by_age.6: Good speech means choosing words that are true, kind, and helpful before you speak.
definition_by_age.8: Qawl sadid means speaking words that are honest, kind, and correct — thinking before speaking so your words help rather than hurt.

learning_objective: Children can pause and choose a kind word instead of an unkind one in a moment of frustration.
notes: New concept file created 2026-08-05 — confirmed via search that no existing concept (self_control, respect_for_parents, kindness) covers general good-speech as its own topic before creating this. No evidence attached yet at creation time, per instruction: create the concept first, attach only independently verified evidence after.

hd_002.reasoning: This hadith IS the good-speech hadith itself ('speak good or remain silent') — it was previously misapplied to concept_honesty as a stretch; here it's a perfect direct match, no new ingestion needed, just correct relinking.

recommended_default.note: Added during v2.17 pilot-production-validation run — real thematic match found in existing conflict_library.json, not fabricated.

alternative_patterns.reasoning: Deciding whether to repeat gossip is a live temptation/choice moment.
An unkind word by accident fits misunderstanding->conversation->reconciliation too.
